title: Replace quest init's yes/no question chain with a multi-select TUI listing supported instruction files
description:
Direct user instruction, relayed and superseding the interaction shape QCLI-254 just shipped (which stays useful: it added the yes/no question chain -- "write instructions?" then "claude or codex?" -- as an improvement over the old single hardcoded AGENTS.md confirm). The user's exact words: "currently there is a series of yes on questions to determine which CLI harness to config. Instead let's replace it with a multi-select TUI. A list of the supported ones and they can select and install the ones they want. backlog.md has a good example."

Reference verified by the orchestrator directly against Backlog.md's source (src/cli.ts ~line 1044): @clack/prompts multiselect, with a message, an options list of {label, value} pairs, required: false, explicit clack.isCancel() handling that exits cleanly rather than throwing, and a non-interactive fallback to AGENTS.md.

Scope, per the orchestrator's explicit instruction: implement the multi-select over quest's two currently-supported targets only -- claude (CLAUDE.md) and codex (AGENTS.md). Do not add gemini or copilot-instructions targets in this change; growing the supported set is a separate, deliberate decision for the user to make, not something to fold in here.

Three things that must not be conflated, per the orchestrator's ruling:
1. Instruction files are not skills. The multi-select chooses which managed instruction blocks to write. Whether .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md is generated stays governed by --skill-source, since in this fleet skills ship from the marketplace -- selecting CLAUDE.md in the multi-select must not re-introduce a generated skill (QCLI-254's --skill-source plugin same-call fix stays exactly as shipped).
2. The non-interactive path must not change: --target's unset default stays codex for scripted callers, unchanged. The multi-select replaces the interactive PROMPT only, not the --target/--agent-instructions flags.
3. --target codex stays fully available as an explicit capability, same reasoning as QCLI-254.

Coordination: this is a shared UX contract with lore-cli, not two independent fixes -- the whole reason the user noticed is that quest init and lore init behaved differently on the same question. Reached out to lore-cli directly to agree the exact shape (message wording, options, cancel behavior) before locking in the quest-cli side, per the orchestrator's instruction to coordinate directly and escalate only on disagreement.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest init's interactive path replaces the yes-then-yes/no question chain (write instructions? then claude or codex?) with a single multi-select listing quest's supported instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md), letting the user tick zero, one, or both

The multi-select's wording, option ordering, and cancel behavior are agreed with lore-cli directly (not decided unilaterally) so quest init and lore init present the same interaction on the same question -- the exact gap the user noticed
Selecting CLAUDE.md alone never writes a skill file -- that stays governed only by --skill-source, unchanged from QCLI-254

The non-interactive path (--agent-instructions, --target, --skill-source flags) is completely unchanged: no --target still defaults to codex for scripted callers, and a non-interactive invocation (no TTY, or an explicit flag already given) never hits the new prompt
Regression tests cover a fake multi-select returning zero files, one file, both files, and a cancel, plus confirm the non-interactive flag path is untouched

plan: 1. Add @clack/prompts as a dependency (done, bun add). Replace InitWizardPrompts' text/confirm-based two-question chain with a text/selectInstructionFiles interface: name and task-ID-prefix stay plain text prompts; a single multiselect replaces write-instructions + which-file.

2. InitWizardAnswers.writeInstructions/target become targets: readonly AgentInstructionTarget[]. runInitWizard returns InitWizardAnswers | undefined (undefined = user cancelled the multiselect), keeping the pure function testable with fake prompts -- no process.exit inside it.

3. Wire a real clack-backed selectInstructionFiles at the dispatcher call site: multiselect({message, options: [claude pre-checked, codex unchecked], required: false}), isCancel() checked explicitly. On cancel, the dispatcher (not the pure wizard function) prints clack's cancel() message and exits 0 -- no partial workspace state, since initializeWorkspace is only ever called after the wizard resolves.

4. Dispatcher: when 0 or 1 targets selected, write instructions/skill exactly as today (byte-identical envelope shape, backward compatible with every --target scripted caller). When 2+ targets selected (only reachable via the interactive wizard), write instructions for each into an additive instructionsByTarget field; skill stays a single write (not per-target) exactly as already shipped in QCLI-254 -- write it once whenever writeInstructions is true and agentSkillSource !== 'plugin', independent of which/how many targets.

5. Pre-check claude only in the multiselect's initialValues, matching QCLI-254's just-shipped bare-Enter default -- agreed with lore-cli as the quest-specific continuation of that ruling (lore pre-checks all available targets per its own availability-detection and OPAG-41 history; different histories, same underlying principle).

6. Regression tests: fake multiselect prompt covering zero/one/both selections and a cancel: rewrite init-wizard.test.ts for the new interface; add a CLI-level bootstrap-process.test.ts-style test is not reachable for the interactive path (no real TTY in CI) -- cover the dispatcher's multi-target write logic and cancel handling via a unit-level seam instead, and confirm the non-interactive/--target flag path's envelope is byte-identical to before.
implementationNotes:
REVERSAL, ruled by the orchestrator (opum-agent) shortly after this task closed: the multiselect's pre-check default changes from claude-only to nothing pre-checked, matching lore-cli's independently-reached revision of its own default. Recording why, so a later reader sees this as a superseding ruling rather than two contradictory records to guess between.

This task's final summary said the claude-only pre-check was "continuing QCLI-254's just-shipped bare-Enter default." That statement is now the thing that reversed. QCLI-254's "if a bare Enter needs a default, make it claude" ruling was conditional on the confirm/either-or interaction shape, where a bare Enter had no choice but to resolve to something (a confirm is binary; an either-or must pick one). This task's own multiselect removed that forcing function: required: false makes "select nothing" a legitimate, already-tested, zero-cost outcome. The premise QCLI-254's ruling depended on no longer holds in the shape this task shipped, so its conclusion does not survive intact into this task's design either, even though it was applied here at implementation time.

The deciding argument, per the orchestrator: the user's own wording was "they can select and install the ones they want" -- active selection, not deselection. Pre-checking anything (claude alone, or lore's original all-available) inverts that into "here is what you are getting, remove what you do not want," which is the same shape as the user's original complaint (files written that nobody asked for).

Follow-up change (small, separate PR per the orchestrator's instruction not to bundle a reversal into the pending promotion): drop the initialValues filter in clackSelectInstructionFiles so a bare Enter resolves to an empty selection, writing nothing -- already exercised by this task's own "selecting nothing is a legal, deliberate answer" test. Coordinated wording with lore-cli before landing so both CLIs present the same default.
finalSummary:
Fixed. quest init's interactive path now presents a single @clack/prompts multiselect (matching Backlog.md's reference shape) instead of the yes/then-yes/no question chain QCLI-254 shipped a few minutes earlier in this same session.

Implementation: InitWizardPrompts' confirm primitive is replaced with selectInstructionFiles; InitWizardAnswers.writeInstructions/target become targets: readonly AgentInstructionTarget[]. runInitWizard now returns InitWizardAnswers | undefined, where undefined means the user cancelled -- distinct from an empty array, which is a legal "write nothing" answer. The dispatcher treats a cancel as a clean exit (exit 0, no output) before initializeWorkspace ever runs, so there is no partial workspace state; clack's own cancel() call prints the message.

Multi-target write logic (0/1/2 files selected) is extracted into a new exported, directly-testable writeInitInstructions() function: the scripted --target path and an interactive selection of exactly one file both keep the EXACT prior single-object instructions/skill envelope shape (byte-identical, verified live and via the unchanged bootstrap-process.test.ts suite -- 22/22 still pass with zero edits needed). An interactive selection of both files (only reachable through the wizard; --target itself still only ever accepts one value) uses a new additive instructionsByTarget field. The skill file write stays governed only by --skill-source, unchanged from QCLI-254, and is written once regardless of how many targets were selected -- not per target.

Pre-check: claude only, continuing QCLI-254's just-shipped bare-Enter default (quest has no availability-detection to key a richer default off of).

Coordination with lore-cli (per the orchestrator's instruction): agreed the exact message wording ("Select instruction files to write (space toggles, enter accepts)"), required: false with empty selection legal, explicit isCancel() handling, and that the multi-select replaces the prompt only, not the flags/non-interactive defaults. lore's three-option set (adds Hermes) and pre-select-all-available default are confirmed as real per-CLI differences (lore has availability detection and an OPAG-41 history quest doesn't), not something to harmonize away.

Regression tests: test/contract/init-wizard.test.ts rewritten for the multiselect interface (name/prefix/multiselect ordering, both-selected, empty-is-legal, cancel-aborts-the-whole-wizard, exact-answer-roundtrip) plus four new tests directly exercising writeInitInstructions against a real temp directory (single scripted target, single interactive target, both targets via instructionsByTarget, and --skill-source plugin skipping the write for both shapes) -- covering the multi-target dispatcher path a spawned-process CLI test cannot reach without a live TTY. test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts required zero changes: all 22 existing tests still pass unmodified, confirming the scripted path is untouched.

command-help.ts's init summary rewritten to describe the multi-select.

bun run check: typecheck/lint/format/layer:check all pass; 440 tests, 0 fail (was 435; +5 net new). 1 pre-existing unrelated lint warning, confirmed present on dev before this branch.
